entities.summary:
Global war originating in Europe, 1914–1918 Took place in Africa. Date: 1914-07-28. Ended: 1918-11-11.

The Great War, as it was known at the time, was a global conflict that involved many of the world's major powers. The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria-Hungary in June 1914 sparked a chain reaction of events that led to the outbreak of war.

The war saw the introduction of new military technologies, including tanks, machine guns, and poison gas, which had a profound impact on the nature of warfare. The war also saw the rise of new global powers, such as the United States, which emerged as a major world power following the war.

The war had a profound impact on the world, leading to the downfall of several empires, including the Austro-Hungarian and German empires, and the redrawing of the map of Europe. The war also led to the rise of new ideologies, such as communism and fascism, which would shape the course of world history in the decades that followed.

The war ended with the Armistice of November 11, 1918, which marked the end of hostilities between the Allied Powers and Germany. The Treaty of Versailles, signed in June 1919, imposed harsh penalties on Germany and contributed to the rise of Nazi Germany in the years leading up to World War II.

The legacy of World War I can still be seen today, with many of the conflicts and tensions that arose during the war continuing to shape global politics and international relations.

entities.summary: Global conflict centered in Europe from 1914 to 1918, triggered by the July Crisis following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand. The war involved over 30 nations, introduced industrialized warfare, and caused approximately 20 million deaths. It reshaped geopolitics, dissolved empires, and set the stage for World War II.
